description:
## Change
- Run the TPC-H cells of the Polars matrix as in pvm-p1 (three measured iterations, seedless, scale factor 10), at a commit that also contains crr-c2. Stage, validate and publish as in pvm-p2.
- In the same core pull request, update _project/analysis/polars-version-matrix/ findings for TPC-H. The blog draft is updated in pvm-p6.
- The results are power-only at a standard scale: ranked in the power-only lane with the derived label.

## Decision gates
- Same heavy-work, validation and no-edit gates as pvm-p1 and pvm-p2.
- Notify the owner when each run starts (owner, 2026-11-24 and decision 11 of 2026-11-25), with the command, maximum run time and log path.
- Every other TPC-H scale factor 10 result is excluded for a known data defect, so the cohort will hold only Polars engine settings. Decision 3 counts engine settings, so the three Polars settings meet the cohort minimum. Say so in CORPUS_NOTES.md. Do not wait for duckdb-sf10-tpch-defective-datagen-rerun.
- If any query fails row-count validation against the crr-c2 reference, stop and report the query; do not publish that result as passed.

## Guardrails (apply to every item of this plan)
- Fix the root cause for every platform and benchmark. No rule, exception, label or test may name a platform or a version matrix. Only the pvm-p* items may name Polars, and only to run and stage that run's files.
- Never edit a stored result file to make it pass. Outcomes change only through the rule.
- Any change to the outcome of a stored result must show in the committed outcome snapshot diff in the same pull request and be explained in its body.
- No new stored class value. No reader may decide anything from benchmark.compliance_class, conformance_class or summary.tpc_metrics.suppressed.
- Paths, line numbers and counts in this plan were read on 2026-11-22 at develop 93f3360. Re-read before editing; report drift, do not guess.
- AGENTS.md applies: linked worktree, one pull request per item, close at the merged pull request, heavy work only through make heavy-run, no live cloud run without owner approval in that task.
- At a decision gate, follow the recorded default. If its stop condition is met, stop and report to the owner. Never substitute a different owner decision.
- Read crr-00-corpus-rule-remediation-plan first: it holds the owner decisions, the rule table and the fault types (T1 to T5).
